A1.justification: The PDFs describe successive versions of the same compositional generation work, renamed from MagicComp to Comp-Attn. Both main texts and appendices are readable, including equations, tables, and image-only figures, and support reliable comparison.

before.justification: v1 reports original generated-video evaluations on T2V-CompBench and VBench, component ablations, inference timings, and qualitative demonstrations.

after.justification: v2 reports original video and image generation evaluations, component ablations, latency measurements, and a manual audit of generated layouts. Appendix B distinguishes reproduced experiments from externally sourced baseline scores.

M1.justification: DLFA's union of prior and adaptive masks and restricted attention is replaced by LAM's additive attention biases, controlled by layout IoU. Adaptive layouts change from prior-size-based top-k thresholding to mean thresholding, and CogVideoX modulation targets only video-to-text attention. By contrast, SAD becoming SCI does not itself change the conditioning calculation: the saliency score complements the former confusion score, preserving the interpolation.

E1.justification: v2 adds compositional image generation on T2I-CompBench and dynamic-attribute evaluation within T2V-CompBench. VBench coverage expands from two object/spatial aspects to its full 16-dimension quality and semantics suite. v1's separate trajectory-control demonstration is no longer included, although v2 still discusses customizable layouts.

E2.justification: Table 1 replaces numerous comparators, including ZeroScope, Latte, and VideoRepair, with methods including Dreamina1.2, Kling-1.0, T2V-Turbo-V2, MAGI-1, and SkyReels-v2. LVD and ViCo remain; DreamRunner leaves the main benchmark comparison but remains in component comparisons. v2 additionally evaluates SEGA, ToMe, VideoGrain, and the image-generation comparators SiamLayout and HybridLayout.

E3.justification: T2V-CompBench changes from 100 to 200 prompts per category, and CogVideoX-2B is replaced by CogVideoX-5B alongside additional Wan configurations. v2 compares LVD, ViCo, and Comp-Attn on shared backbones, with shared layouts for LVD. It reports intervention during the first 20% of denoising, versus v1's 10% rule for DLFA, and changes hardware from A100 to H100. Layout planning changes from ChatGLM-4 with 13 planned keyframes to GPT-4o-mini with four keyframes and interpolation.

E4.justification: v2 revises component ablations and adds an explicit removal test for IoU guidance, a fixed-interpolation coefficient sweep, and a manual layout-error analysis covering 1,400 prompts. The interpolation sweep extends v1's direct Word Swap control rather than introducing an entirely unrelated comparison. Appendix F newly tests dense versus sparse layout planning and distinguishes motion and size errors.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run counts, random seeds, confidence intervals, error bars, or statistical significance tests. v2's layout-error frequencies are additional empirical outcomes, not uncertainty estimates for the reported generation results.

E6.justification: The benchmark and ablation results are substantially replaced and expanded. Newly reported within-v2 comparisons include Wan2.2's T2V-CompBench average increasing from 0.5742 to 0.6414 with Comp-Attn, FLUX's image-generation average from 0.5819 to 0.6131, and layout-error rates of 2.93% versus 1.14%. These are new comparisons, not matched v1-to-v2 performance gains; backbone and evaluation settings changed.

T1.justification: The attention formalization is substantially revised: v1's size-derived thresholds, mask unions, and supplementary block-mask equations are replaced by mean-threshold layouts and signed, IoU-weighted attention-bias definitions in v2 Equations 4–12. This changes the mathematical operator, not merely notation. The complementary confusion/saliency formulations remain equivalent, and neither version introduces theorems or proofs.

C1.justification: The central contribution changes from dual-phase semantic disambiguation and fused layout masking to a composition-aware cross-attention variant using subject presence and relational alignment. The abstract and conclusion expand the main applicability claim to compositional image generation and foreground Wan results, while no longer foregrounding trajectory control. Training-free operation and model independence remain core claims.

C2.justification: v2 adds substantive explanations for IoU feedback, preservation of general video quality, context-dependent interpolation, and tolerance of imperfect layouts. Appendix F explains motion/size planning failures and why sparse keyframes help. Conversely, v1's explicit caveats about ambiguous prompts, precise trajectories, and frame-level temporal control disappear; the general dependence on backbone capabilities remains.

D1.justification: v2 adds architecture-specific adaptation instructions, baseline-result provenance, shared-layout information, API cost and latency, and a revised planning template. However, it removes v1's explicit sampler, denoising-step, guidance-scale, resolution, and frame-count table, as well as its project-page link. These substantially change reproducibility documentation; removal of the link does not establish that the resource became unavailable.

R1.justification: Related work is repositioned around complementary shortcomings of layout control and inference-time optimization, extending the discussion from video to compositional visual generation. New substantive references include SEGA, Attend-and-Excite, ConceptAttention, Wan, autoregressive diffusion methods, and recent layout-to-image approaches. This changes the methodological context and novelty argument beyond bibliographic updates.

P1.justification: The title, abstract, introduction, related work, and substantial method and results passages are rewritten around the Present-and-Align narrative. SAD/DLFA terminology becomes SCI/LAM, the standalone Applications section disappears, and the supplement is reorganized into Appendices A–G. The changes constitute extensive narrative restructuring, beyond text added for new experiments.

P2.justification: The overview and architecture diagrams are redrawn, and the similarity and mask-fusion illustrations are replaced by attention-response and distribution analyses. The main comparison table is reorganized into backbone-specific groups, with separate VBench, image-generation, latency, and diagnostic tables. Appendix galleries are regrouped by model, and the layout prompt is redesigned as a planning/interpolation diagram.

improvement.justification: v2 substantially strengthens the evidence supporting effectiveness and applicability: shared-backbone comparisons reduce confounding, full VBench evaluation checks quality tradeoffs, and targeted ablations plus the layout audit investigate mechanisms and failures that v1 leaves weakly tested. Image-generation experiments support the broader applicability claim. These gains outweigh the loss of explicit hyperparameters and remaining overstatements, such as the broad LAM-superiority interpretation despite VideoGrain's higher Interaction score in Table 6.
